title: Cardiovascular and Renal Protection With SGLT Inhibition in Kidney Transplant Recipients: The RENAISSANCE Trial
official: Cardiovascular and Renal Protection With SGLT Inhibition in Kidney Transplant Recipients (RENAISSANCE): A Randomized, Placebo-controlled, Double Blinded, Multicenter Clinical Trial of Sotagliflozin Versus Placebo
summary: This study will examine whether sotagliflozin, a medication that may protect the heart and kidneys, can improve long-term health in people who have received a kidney transplant. The study will compare sotagliflozin with an inactive placebo in approximately 900 adult kidney transplant recipients. Researchers will assess whether the medication can reduce the risk of kidney transplant failure, worsening kidney function, heart problems, stroke, heart attack, heart failure, and death. The study will also closely monitor participants for possible side effects, including infections, dehydration, fractures, and rejection of the transplanted kidney.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. ≥ 6 months post living or deceased donor kidney transplant
3. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥20 ml/min/1.73m2 by the CKD-EPI-creatinine 2021 formula within 28 days prior to randomization.
4. At increased risk for worsening allograft function or cardiovascular event as defined by one of the following groups:

   1. Type 2 diabetes
   2. Body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m2
   3. History of post-kidney transplant hospitalization for congestive heart failure (regardless of ejection fraction)
   4. eGFR \<30 ml/min/1.73m2
   5. Albuminuria (UACR ≥ 11.3 mg/mmol or urine protein to creatinine ratio (UPCR) ≥ 500 mg/g) within 28 days of randomization and a second urine sample over the prior two years; the rationale for this cut-point is that given the patient-centered study design, we are not necessitating first morning voids and random urine specimen albumins are usually higher than first morning samples.
   6. History of CV event (myocardial infarction, stroke)
   7. At risk for CV event (history of coronary artery bypass, percutaneous coronary intervention, peripheral artery bypass or stent, or age ≥50yr (men) or ≥60yr (women) with at least two additional risk factors: hypertension, hyperlipidemia or current smoker (see MOP for definitions of hypertension and hyperlipidemia).
5. Ability of the participant or Legally Authorized Representative to understand and sign a written informed consent.
6. Ability to comply with all components of the study

Exclusion Criteria:

1. SGLT inhibitor use in the previous 3 months
2. Type 1 diabetes
3. Multi-organ or extrarenal transplant (except cornea)
4. Acute coronary syndrome, transient ischemic attack or stroke within 1 month prior to screening
5. Suspicion for acute rejection and/or plans for kidney biopsy
6. Acute rejection within 3 months prior to screening
7. Ongoing treatment for rejection
8. Acute kidney injury (AKI) in the last 3 months (may be rescreened)
9. History of diabetic ketoacidosis in the last 5 years
10. High risk for urinary tract infection (UTI) (e.g. need for indwelling or recurrent catheterization, or frequent (\>3 per year) UTIs)
11. Active treatment for BK nephropathy, Cytomegalovirus viremia, Epstein Barr Virus viremia
12. Active immunosuppressive treatment for recurrent/post-transplant glomerulonephritis
13. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C)
14. Current treatment with rifampicin
15. Pregnancy, lactation or women of child-bearing potential\* unless taking adequate precautions to avoid the possibility of becoming pregnant (as defined in the manual of procedures) until 4 weeks after the last dose of study drug
16. Known allergic reactions to components of sotagliflozin
17. Current treatment with another investigational drug or device
18. Incarcerated individuals
19. History of any other acute or chronic medical condition (e.g., urogenital abnormalities) or pre-planned surgical procedure that in the opinion of the investigator would compromise the safety of the patient or the integrity of the study results.

    * A woman of child-bearing potential is defined as a participant who has:

      * Experienced menarche and engages in activity that involves penile-vaginal intercourse with a partner capable of causing pregnancy AND
      * Has not undergone surgical sterilization (hysterectomy, bilateral salpingectomy/oophorectomy) or is not postmenopausal (≥12 consecutive months of spontaneous amenorrhea without an alternative medical cause).
